correctness.rationale: Stationary balance gives the reported probabilities for positive rates, and differentiation gives the reported quartic with the stated negative prefactor. Independent symbolic computation recovers both discriminants and the coprimality certificate; an exact Sturm count gives one positive, simple zero of the septic. At r=1/100 the quartic signs at 0, sqrt(r)=1/10, 1/5 and 1 are −,+,−,+; at r=1 Descartes gives one positive root. A root cannot cross 0 or sqrt(r) (the quartic is strictly negative at the former and positive at the latter), or escape at a finite r>0. The two roots above sqrt(r) therefore merge at the discriminant zero into a double root, with the lower root simple; the double zero of D' gives a stationary inflection. The exact r/x reflection dominates every x>sqrt(r), and sqrt(r) itself has nonzero derivative. The single lower maximum is globally unique. The two-stage formula gives one peak. Exact bracket (0.0817033790460166, 0.0817033790460167): the printed decimal is correctly rounded, not a truncation.
